section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the correlations between character strengths and various emotional vulnerabilities and positive psychological processes. It reports that character strengths were negatively correlated with anger (rs = -.29 to -.61), loneliness (rs = -.28 to -.51), and depressive symptoms (rs = -.31 to -.53). Additionally, character strengths were positively correlated with acceptance (rs = .25 to .58), self-compassion (rs = .35 to .68), and perspective taking (rs = .25 to .44), showing unique correlations with aspects of empathy.
section_summary.evidence_source: 4.3. Character strengths, emotional vulnerabilities, and positive psychological processes Character strengths were negatively correlated with emotional vulnerabilities including anger (rs = -.29 to -.61), loneliness (rs = -.28 to -.51) and depressive symptoms (rs = -.31 to -.53). Strengths were positively correlated with acceptance (rs = .25 to .58), self-compassion (rs = .35 to .68) and perspective taking (rs = .25 to .44) but demonstrated unique correlations with aspects of empathy.
